text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The opposition alliance proposes a government structure with a president, prime minister and vice presidents to share power.
- Kenya Railways signs an agreement with Caltex oil company to rehabilitate 10 tank wagons for its exclusive use.
- A non-governmental organisation based in Nairobi starts a comprehensive education programme to rehabilitate street children.

- A government doctor at a maximum security prison allegedly threatens to administer forcibly anti-depressants to jailed former Nakuru member of parliament Koigi wa Wamwere and two other people convicted with him.
- Opposition FORD-Kenya Langata member of parliament Raila Odinga says people should have a say in the constitution reform debate because it is a contract between them and the rulers.
- Kenya receives 431 million shillings as additional assistance for various projects from the U.S. government.
- Kenya Wildlife Service translocates a total of 70 hirola antelopes but five are pronounced dead on arrival at Tsavo National Park.
